intent.skill_expression: reading character tells, collectible optimization, split-party Adventure Mode management, chaos deployment timing

secondary_metrics: regular relationship scores (Teddy, Mort, Mike, etc.)
compounding_mechanisms: burger quality → satisfaction → reputation → regular visits → passive buffs → Belcher Rating → ingredient/equipment unlocks → burger quality ceiling rises
family morale decay → service quality drops → customer dissatisfaction → regular absence → passive buff loss → revenue decline → ingredient degradation → Belcher Rating sink
chaos layer — Tina/Gene/Louise mood states affect operations; manageable by default, deployable as high-risk gambits
Burger of the Day — daily creativity modifier sets performance ceiling for the session
Mr. Fischoeder rent pressure — persistent financial floor stressor
irreversible_actions: regular relationship burned — very difficult recovery path (dedicated quest chain + grand gesture cost)
family schism event — member checks out, debuffs until repaired
recipe lost — specific Burger of the Day combinations unrecoverable without recipe book system
Fischoeder escalation — missed rent ratchets terms permanently upward
neighborhood event resolution — player choices permanently reshape neighborhood state
system_spine.loss_condition: soft fail — declining Belcher Rating compounds difficulty, no termination
system_spine.collapse_behavior: degraded state compounds difficulty across all variables simultaneously
system_spine.collapse_recovery: baseline grind + crisis mode unique mechanics + community rally accelerant (gated by active regular relationships)

core_loops.loop_30s: burger crafting (primary) + chaos intercept (disruptor) + ingredient management (micro-scarcity) + Bob internal monologue capture (recipe system feed)
core_loops.loop_5m: simultaneous layered objectives — survive customer rush wave + progress regular quest + hit Burger of the Day target + steer active chaos event toward outcome
core_loops.loop_60m: one rush completed + partial regular quest progress + potential neighborhood event trigger + Fischoeder appearance (pressure/opportunity punctuation)
decision_points: deploy vs. manage a kid — gambit or stability
accept Fischoeder's terms vs. resist — short-term relief vs. long-term cost
Burger of the Day creativity vs. safety — high ceiling/risk vs. stable modifier
intervene in neighborhood event vs. let it play out — control vs. emergent outcome
call family meeting — morale/focus restoration at cost of service momentum, diminishing returns if overused

adventure_mode.function: relationship building + resource gathering + neighborhood exploration
adventure_mode.party_model: split party — assign family members to parallel activities
adventure_mode.feeds_back_into: restaurant performance, quest progression, event intel, ingredient supply

list: adventure mode action time (per family member per day off)
Borobu cards (Louise — variable function per card)
Chunky Blast-Offs (Gene — variable function per item, Ken activation currency)
resources.flows_text: money↔ingredients standard flow; collectibles tradeable with NPCs; Gene spends Blast-Offs to activate Ken (hidden buff source); recipe selling triggers Bob morale cost; relationship score spendable for short-term gain at long-term cost; collectibles enter via Adventure Mode exploration + customer drops + vendor purchase + quest rewards, tiered by rarity
resources.scarcity_model: ingredients tiered by rarity — common always available, rare raises Burger of the Day quality ceiling, legendary gates specific recipes entirely

liquidity_layer.convertibility_rules: money↔ingredients, collectibles tradeable with NPCs, Gene spends Blast-Offs to activate Ken, recipe selling triggers Bob morale cost, relationship score spendable for short-term gain at long-term cost
liquidity_layer.leverage_rules: Ken buffs unacknowledged by other family systems — wildcard layer

ingredient supply levels — visible not spoilage timing
kid chaos state — visible mood, not active scheme
neighborhood event pressure — something building, specifics hidden

mystery_mechanics.how_players_learn: progressive tell recognition, pattern matching across runs, some mechanics permanently ambiguous
permanent_mysteries: Ken's true nature — intentionally never resolved
Fischoeder's full agenda — locked until system expansion

misinformation.how: Louise can feed player bad intel as part of active scheme; Fischoeder offers obscure real intentions — deception tied to specific characters

yips_mechanic.trigger: stress-triggered with random variance — Fischoeder presence, low family morale, health inspection proximity raise probability
yips_mechanic.effect: Bob's burger quality score temporarily degraded, spiral risk activated
yips_mechanic.recovery: accumulative encouragement threshold — weighted sum of encouraging events from any present source

black_swan_events.trigger_model: hybrid — random low-probability events, pressure-buildup triggers, and telegraphed incoming events with unknown specifics

pressure_engine.collapse_behavior: degraded state compounds difficulty across all variables simultaneously
pressure_engine.collapse_recovery: baseline grind + crisis mode unique mechanics + community rally accelerant (gated by active regular relationships)

dominant_strategy_risks: restaurant-only grind ignoring Adventure Mode — naturally punished by ingredient/relationship decay
Louise gambit over-deployment — needs diminishing returns mechanic
Blast-Off hoarding — needs Gene restlessness mechanic to discourage
anti_runaway_leader_mechanics: high Belcher Rating scales up incoming pressure — harder inspections, bigger Fischoeder schemes, more Pesto interference
legendary ingredients have spoilage timer — prevents stockpiling
regular relationships decay passively — no coasting on accumulated goodwill

positive: burger quality → satisfaction → reputation → regular visits → passive buffs → Belcher Rating → unlocks → burger quality ceiling rises
negative: morale decay → service drops → dissatisfaction → regular absence → buff loss → revenue decline → ingredient degradation → Belcher Rating sink
mixed: chaos deployment — high risk/reward, outcome dependent on timing and kid state
recipe selling — short-term revenue, long-term Bob morale cost
family meeting — morale restoration with diminishing returns
high Rating → scaled pressure — success is never safe

tipping_points: Fischoeder escalation tier 3 — rent becomes existential
two regulars burned simultaneously — community rally collapses
Louise + Linda simultaneous chaos — service unmanageable without family meeting
exploit_countermeasures: Ken wildcard buffs unverifiable — prevents perfect optimization
misinformation layer via Louise and Fischoeder
Gene restlessness mechanic — discourages Blast-Off hoarding
scaled pressure at high Rating — no safe plateau

content_replay.variety_source: Burger of the Day combinatorial system + rotating regular quest pool + permanent neighborhood state changes + procedural chaos scheme combinations + asymmetric collectible builds

what_persists: recipe book — discovered recipes permanent unless sold
regular relationship scores — burned relationships carry forward
Fischoeder escalation tier — rent ratchet never resets
neighborhood state — resolved events permanently alter world
persistence.why_it_matters: every session builds or damages a world state that never fully resets — decisions have permanent weight

unlocks: new equipment and ingredients at Belcher Rating thresholds
permanent passive buffs from completed regular quest arcs
character-specific gambits from collectible set completion
Adventure Mode locations expand with Rating
Fischoeder agenda chapters at escalation thresholds
rule_mutators: completed neighborhood events permanently alter available customer pool
burned regulars remove their passive buff from the game permanently until recovered
recipe book size scales — more recipes discovered, more Burger of the Day options available daily

burger crafting — 3 ingredient tiers, basic quality scoring
one regular (Teddy) — relationship meter, one quest type, passive buff when present
basic chaos layer — Louise only, one gambit type
Fischoeder rent clock — appears at session end, single escalation tier
Burger of the Day — creativity vs. safety choice at session start
Belcher Rating as visible composite score
family morale as single tracked variable
Bob's yips — stress-triggered, accumulative encouragement threshold recovery
success_metrics: player makes at least 3 meaningful decisions per rush wave
Teddy presence creates noticeable mechanical difference
Louise chaos event creates genuine tension at least once per session
Fischoeder appearance feels like earned pressure not random punishment
Burger of the Day choice feels consequential by end of rush

pillars: Chaos is the point — pressure, disruption, and imperfection are features not bugs
Family first, restaurant second — relationships always matter more than the score
Every burger tells a story — creativity, risk, and Bob's identity embedded in every crafting decision
do_list: make every Burger of the Day feel like a creative act with Bob's voice
let family moments land emotionally even when mechanically inconvenient
make Teddy's presence genuinely matter every session
dont_list: let the player feel fully optimized
make Louise's gambits feel like interruptions
sacrifice character authenticity for mechanical convenience
make Belcher Rating the only thing the player cares about
